issue_text: verdictForCounts' escalation guard `if blocking && attemptNumber >= maxAttempts` (and the whole ESCALATED branch, lines 907-910) is not pinned by any test in the pr-ready gate. The only unit call is verdictForCounts(counts, "gate", 1, 3) with zero blocking findings (review_markdown_test.go:35, TestVerdictForNonBlockingFindingsIsPassAdvisory), which returns PASS_ADVISORY and never touches this branch. The integration fixtures (shardedRepo) always block at attempt 1 of 3 (TestGCOnlyRunsAfterAPassingGate asserts result.Blocking with NEEDS_REVISION), so the escalation path is never exercised end-to-end either. The whole `if blocking && attemptNumber >= maxAttempts { ESCALATED }` block could be deleted, or `>=` inverted to `>` (an off-by-one that would grant one extra attempt / fail to escalate at exactly maxAttempts), and every test in the repo still passes.

The final `return "PASS", "passed", false, ""` in verdictForCounts (line 917) is unreachable by any test. Reaching it requires gateEffect=="gate" (only set when report.Capabilities.Beads || .Metaswarm, review.go:176) AND all finding counts zero. Every prready Create test builds a plain temp git repo (shardedRepo, shardwiring_test.go:70) with no Beads/metaswarm capability, so gateEffect is always "advisory" and line 914 (`gateEffect=="advisory" || nonBlocking`) always returns PASS_ADVISORY first. Changing line 917 from "PASS" to "PASS_ADVISORY" (collapsing the clean-gate-mode verdict into advisory) leaves all tests green.

readEvidence truncates by raw byte count: `if len(text) > 12000 { return text[:12000] }`. This slices at a byte boundary and can split a multi-byte UTF-8 rune, emitting an invalid trailing byte into evidenceText, which is then embedded verbatim into the context-pack markdown (contextMarkdown line 889) and passed to reviewers. readEvidence is only 22.2% covered and the truncation branch is untested, so nothing checks the truncation preserves valid UTF-8 or cuts on a rune boundary.
